feedback: The candidate changes one variable from the best raced design, iteration 5 (kp 7.0, kd 0.6, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction). kp goes from 7.0 to 6.5, and kd, geometry, base_speed, ki and line_loss stay the same. Iteration 5 scored 107.76 and still ran off track on all 60 trials. Its oval steering_oscillation was 0.250, above the 0.2 concern level, and the same value at kd 0.4 showed that more kd had stopped helping. Oval max_error was 0.063, just over the 0.06 limit. Line losses were 1.2 on the oval, 1.65 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom. Progress was 0.49, 0.22 and 0.08. Body width cannot relax the off-track limit, so control has to fix it. This follows the plan from iteration 5: when oscillation stays above 0.2 at kd 0.6, reduce kp rather than add more kd. Nothing here states how this candidate will perform. It is a single-variable, well-supported step from the best raced design, and this is the middle of the race with 5 iterations left after this one, so approve it to race and get per-track telemetry. After the race: if oval steering_oscillation is now at or below 0.2 but max_error is still at or above 0.06, widen geometry.sensor_positions to x = ±0.040 m with 16 mm sensors and test kp near 8.0 with kd 0.6. If oscillation is still above 0.2 at kp 6.5, reduce kd toward 0.5 and keep kp 6.5, because more damping has not reduced oscillation. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more at the same bend entries, test line_loss search_left or search_right, choosing the side the failing bends turn towards, and raise base_speed toward 1.6 only if progress is still below 1 with max_error under 0.06.
